intent: Implement, only after explicit phase approval, a provenance-backed and non-destructive Project Orchestrator update system covering Git-native Launch Pad guidance and additive, safe-all, and selective updates for generated projects without committing, pushing, publishing, deploying, or mutating external systems.

steps.action: Map managed update assets, ownership scopes, skill dependency closure, generated companions, and affected consumers before changing update contracts.
inputs: pso.mjs update, adoption, creation, verification, and transaction paths
outputs: Dependency-closed capability bundle and managed-asset impact map
completionCriteria: Every framework skill has a deterministic transitive dependency closure and generated help companion.
Whole-file, directory, generated-file, and managed-region ownership scopes are distinguished from project-owned paths.
Affected creation, adoption, update, verification, profile, schema, and report consumers are identified with no unresolved cycle or missing owner.
steps.rollback: No rollback is required because this step is read-only analysis; preserve the prior valid dependency reports if regeneration fails.
steps.recovery: Correct incomplete inventory or ownership evidence and rerun the same dependency analysis before migration planning.

steps.action: Define the versioned manifest, baseline lock, update-plan, selection, compatibility, migration, and rollback contracts for safe three-way updates.
inputs: Current adoption plan and verification report shapes
Current transaction journal and backup behavior
completionCriteria: The design records normalized per-file SHA-256 baselines, source framework identity, ownership scope, and track, pin, or fork policy without absolute source paths or secrets.
The three-way classifier covers unchanged, upstream-only, local-only, converged, diverged, added, deleted, and legacy-unknown states.
Schema 1.0 consumers remain readable while schema 1.1 manifest and lock creation, adoption, update, downgrade, backup, and rollback behavior is explicit.
Legacy projects with no lock bootstrap only byte-equivalent assets and preserve every differing asset as unknown or customized pending an explicit decision.
steps.rollback: Reject the candidate migration design and preserve schema 1.0 behavior and reports.
steps.recovery: Resolve any consumer, compatibility, or rollback gap and regenerate the migration plan before approval.

steps.action: Review and explicitly approve the exact local implementation phase, public CLI compatibility rules, contract changes, and bounded file list.
inputs: Proposed implementation files and public CLI examples
outputs: Approved CLI, schema, test, and documentation boundary
completionCriteria: Approval names the exact implementation boundary and confirms that bare pso update means safe all-mode, never force replacement.
Approval confirms additive, all, and select behavior plus track, pin, fork, keep, replace, and exact-asset force semantics.
Commit, push, publication, deployment, release, remote fetch, and external mutation remain separately prohibited.
steps.rollback: Withdraw approval before implementation starts; no source artifacts are changed by this gate.
steps.recovery: Record rejected or narrowed requirements in a new clarification and workflow-plan lineage rather than inferring approval.

steps.action: Implement baseline provenance capture and the pure three-way asset classifier through focused red-green tests.
inputs: tests/adoption-rerun.test.mjs neighboring creation and adoption fixtures
outputs: Failing then passing provenance and classifier tests
Versioned project manifest and baseline lock schemas
completionCriteria: Creation and adoption record canonical normalized-text hashes for every managed file and file within a managed directory.
Line-ending normalization prevents false local modifications across supported Windows and Unix checkouts.
The complete base, local, and upstream state matrix is covered by behavior-level tests, including local or upstream deletion and equal convergence.
Project-owned files and untracked local skills never enter the managed lock implicitly.
steps.rollback: Restore the schema 1.0 manifest writer and remove only the newly introduced lock, schemas, classifier, and focused tests from this slice.
steps.recovery: Keep the correctly failing test, record the implementation blocker, and route through terminal handoff if the baseline contract cannot be made deterministic.

steps.action: Split update planning from adoption and implement additive, safe-all, and selective plans with deterministic dependency closure and automation-safe selection input.
outputs: Versioned project update-plan and selection schemas
Dedicated update plan builder and reports
Interactive selection and equivalent noninteractive CLI inputs
completionCriteria: An unqualified pso update resolves to mode all and dry-run remains mutation-free.
Additive mode installs only absent upstream capability bundles, their missing transitive skill dependencies, generated help, and absent required schemas without overwriting existing content.
Select mode accepts skills and exact asset selectors interactively on a TTY and through a versioned selection file in noninteractive runs; empty noninteractive selection fails closed.
All-mode plans every applicable tracked asset but sets canApply false while any conflict or required compatibility decision remains unresolved.
Portable JSON reports omit source-machine absolute paths and embedded file content.
steps.rollback: Remove the dedicated update planner and retain the existing adoption planner; preserve the passing provenance slice for independent review.
steps.recovery: Reduce the failing mode to one classifier or closure case, repair that behavior, and rerun the same focused suite before continuing.

steps.action: Implement track, pin, and fork policy plus explicit keep, replace, fork, and exact-asset force conflict resolutions without silent local-data loss.
inputs: skill-update exact-target and approval requirements for skill forks
outputs: Failing then passing policy and conflict-resolution tests
Policy persistence in the baseline lock
Skill fork and exact-asset replacement plan actions
completionCriteria: Track is the default only for framework-installed assets; pin preserves the installed baseline and reports available upstream changes.
Fork requires an exact new project-owned skill ID and preserves the local package before restoring the canonical tracked framework skill and regenerating affected help or references.
Keep records an explicit pin or project-owned disposition rather than pretending the local content equals upstream.
Replace and force replacement require exact asset selectors, fresh destination-state preconditions, risk acceptance, and backup; no force-all shortcut exists.
Unresolved or invalid resolutions leave the plan non-applicable and make no project mutation.
steps.rollback: Restore the pre-resolution lock and every backed-up selected asset; never remove a successfully preserved project-owned fork during rollback.
steps.recovery: Discard only the invalid resolution plan, retain local files unchanged, and require a newly generated plan with exact selectors.

steps.action: Integrate safe update application with locks, stale-plan checks, transaction journaling, backups, rollback, verification, and dedicated update evidence.
inputs: Current prepareAdoptionTransaction, applyAdoptionLocked, rollbackAdoptionTransaction, and verifyInstallation behavior
outputs: Failing then passing transactional update tests
Atomic update apply and rollback implementation
completionCriteria: No action is written when the plan is stale, unresolved, outside the managed root, or inconsistent with its recorded base and destination hashes.
The transaction snapshots the manifest, lock, selected managed assets, generated companions, and update reports before the first write.
Interruption or verification failure restores pre-update content and policy state and leaves a recoverable terminal journal.

Verification evaluates selected dependency closure, pins, forks, profile conformance, manifest-lock consistency, and absence of legacy IDs without requiring every pinned asset to equal current upstream.
Adoption reports retain adoption semantics while updates emit dedicated update plan and verification evidence.
steps.rollback: Use the existing journaled reverse-order restore path extended to the manifest, lock, generated companions, update reports, and every selected asset.
steps.recovery: Run the existing recovery command against the terminal transaction journal before generating any new update plan.

steps.action: Implement conservative legacy bootstrap, upstream removal handling, and backward-compatible CLI diagnostics through red-green migration and fuzz tests.
inputs: Legacy skill ID and duplicate-command fixtures
outputs: Failing then passing legacy migration tests
Failing then passing selector, path, symlink, and malformed-lock fuzz tests
Upstream deprecation and removal decision actions
completionCriteria: A legacy asset equal to current upstream can be adopted as the current baseline without a content write.
A legacy asset differing from current upstream is marked legacy-unknown and preserved until keep, replace, or fork is explicitly selected.
Upstream deletion or retirement never deletes a local asset by default and requires an exact reviewed removal action with backup.
Malformed locks, traversal selectors, symlink escapes, duplicate identities, and stale selection files fail closed.
Existing dry-run, JSON, risk-acceptance, and force-templates command behavior remains compatible outside the new update options.
steps.rollback: Restore the pre-bootstrap manifest and omit the new lock when migration cannot complete; all legacy content remains in place.
steps.recovery: Emit a blocked migration report naming each unknown asset and the exact non-destructive operator choices available.

steps.action: Validate the implemented artifact migration, compatibility matrix, forward cutover, downgrade behavior, backup completeness, and rollback evidence.
inputs: STEP-008 passing migration and fuzz evidence
Implemented schemas, manifest writer, lock writer, and update reports
completionCriteria: Every supported producer and consumer combination is passed, blocked, or unsupported with deterministic evidence.
Forward migration and rollback restore tests pass for clean, customized, pinned, forked, interrupted, and legacy-unknown fixtures.
No cutover-ready conclusion is issued if a baseline, compatibility, backup, or restore gap remains.
steps.rollback: Reject the migration candidate and preserve the last valid implementation checkpoint without changing external projects.
steps.recovery: Return to the first failing red-green slice and repeat migration validation after repair.

steps.action: Recompute skill and artifact dependency closure against the implemented catalog, profiles, generated companions, pins, and fork rules.
inputs: All skill contracts and conformance profiles
completionCriteria: Additive and selective bundles are dependency-closed for every conformance profile.
Pins or forks that would violate a required dependency or profile produce a blocking compatibility result.
No cycle, missing skill, ambiguous owner, or orphaned generated companion remains.
steps.rollback: Preserve the prior valid graph and keep the implementation blocked from candidate preparation.
steps.recovery: Repair the catalog, profile, or dependency declaration responsible for the inconsistency and rerun this step.

steps.action: Document generated-project update modes and policies plus a Git-native, validation-first Launch Pad update procedure that never hides merge semantics.
inputs: STEP-010 validated commands, contracts, and closure rules
outputs: Launch Pad Git fetch, inspect, integrate, validate, and rollback procedure
Generated-project additive, all, select, pin, fork, resolution, migration, and recovery examples
completionCriteria: Launch Pad guidance keeps Git authoritative, requires an explicit external action before fetch, and never performs merge, reset, commit, push, or release implicitly.
Generated-project examples show dry-run first, safe-all compatibility, additive dependency closure, interactive and noninteractive selection, and exact conflict resolution.
Documentation states that legacy-unknown assets are preserved, update-all is not force-all, and recovery must complete before replanning after interruption.
Commands and report names exactly match current executable behavior.
steps.rollback: Restore the prior documentation views if implementation commands or contracts are withdrawn.
steps.recovery: Correct mismatched examples from verified CLI output and rerun documentation validation.

steps.action: Review the bounded update-system diff for data loss, compatibility regressions, unsafe selectors, incomplete dependency closure, migration gaps, and missing tests.
inputs: Focused red-green, migration, dependency, fuzz, and repository validation evidence
completionCriteria: No unresolved critical or high-severity defect or local-data-loss path remains.
Every changed contract surface has corresponding tests and documentation.
The review distinguishes the known unrelated audit-checkpoint failure from update-system regressions and records all residual risk.
steps.rollback: No source rollback is performed by this read-only review; preserve prior review evidence if regeneration fails.
steps.recovery: Return to the owning red-green or documentation step for each confirmed finding and repeat the bounded review.

steps.action: Prepare a minimal validated candidate boundary and commit summary without committing, pushing, publishing, deploying, or releasing.
inputs: Current focused and full repository validation evidence
completionCriteria: Every proposed path maps to the approved update-system objective and unrelated generated churn is excluded.
Focused tests and npm run check are current, with any unrelated baseline failure explicitly isolated and not waived.
No commit, push, publication, deployment, release, or external mutation has occurred.
steps.rollback: Discard only newly generated candidate-preparation artifacts; preserve implementation and user-owned changes for review.
steps.recovery: Return to STEP-012 whenever the path boundary, implementation, or validation evidence changes.

steps.action: Publish terminal continuity for completed, blocked, failed, or approval-waiting update-system work with one exact next action.
inputs: Any blocker, failure, rejected approval, or residual-risk evidence
completionCriteria: The handoff records completed, pending, blocked, and failed work without treating planning or phase approval as commit, push, release, or deployment approval.
The latest validation, migration, rollback, and local-change preservation evidence is traceable.
Exactly one next eligible action is identified and the unrelated P4 lineage remains historical rather than silently completed or cancelled.
steps.rollback: Preserve the last valid handoff and regenerate only the mutable continuity views from accepted evidence.
steps.recovery: Rebuild synchronized continuity from the latest valid checkpoint and append-only event history.
